A goaltending coaching academy needed to win local search against five named competitors — and, midway through the engagement, needed its site rescued from a bot-driven hosting suspension that had taken it fully offline.

The challenge

  • Under-optimized for local & AI-driven search against 5 named competitors
  • A legacy content migration had silently hidden the drill library from Google
  • Mid-engagement: a large-scale bot scraping operation triggered a full hosting suspension

What I did

  • Rewrote Rank Math titles & meta descriptions across 10 core pages
  • Implemented LocalBusiness, SportsCoach & Course schema, with VideoObject autodetection
  • Migrated DNS to Cloudflare with zero email downtime, then hardened it with WAF & rate limiting

The hidden drill library

A May 2026 migration had silently set every real drill page (~38 posts) to No Index, Schema Off as a pre-launch default that was never reverted — effectively invisible to Google for months.

Fix (Aug 22): Bulk-restored all Drill posts to Index via Rank Math, applied Course schema at the post-type level, and deployed a dedicated Cloudflare cache rule on /goalie-drills/ to keep the newly-reindexed content fast under renewed crawler traffic.

Incident: the bot attack

What started as a routine SEO engagement became full incident response when a sustained scraping operation escalated into a hosting-level suspension.

Aug 19, 11:09pm
AlertSiteGround detects a DoS pattern — ~195K hits in 24h — and temporarily restricts site access.
Aug 20, ~7:30am
Confirmed downFull account-level suspension. Log review finds scraper requests hitting instant 429s from just 2 distinct JA4 TLS fingerprints across hundreds of source IPs — centralized bot tooling, not organic traffic.
Aug 21
ActionDiagnosed a DNS misconfiguration blocking the Cloudflare migration (DKIM/DMARC CNAMEs proxied instead of DNS-only), fixed it, and completed the nameserver switch — Google Workspace mail verified intact throughout.
Aug 21
ResolvedEscalated directly with SiteGround support with root cause and mitigation already documented. Suspension lifted, live site restored.
Aug 22
HardenedDeployed a second WAF rule targeting the drill-taxonomy scraper pattern, plus rate limiting (20 req / 10s per IP) across the shop and drill sections.
Root-cause insight — two "unrelated" incidents four months apart (a June execution-quota spike and August's suspension) traced back to the same class of problem: uncached, parameterized shop/drill URLs being replayed at scale by automated tooling. Fixing the caching and edge rules — not just the symptoms — is what closed the loop.

Outcome

Visibility restored~38 drill pages back in the index with proper schema after months invisible to search.
Search foundation modernizedMetadata, local, and structured-data groundwork in place across core pages.
Site reliabilityFull recovery from an account-level suspension, with layered Cloudflare defenses now standing guard.
Zero-downtime migrationNo email downtime during the DNS cutover to Cloudflare.
